steps.text: Confirm the EIA Midwest diesel series and that EIA has no Indiana series, then fetch the EIA history data and save the raw rows to disk.
steps.do: 1) web_search to confirm series EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG, its URL, and that EIA has no Indiana state diesel series; note the source date. 2) fetch_url the EIA history page (and the prior-year page if the window spans two years). 3) Immediately use local:Write to save the fetched weekly rows (date, price) verbatim to eia_raw_midwest.txt, so nothing is lost to context truncation. Read files back only with local:Read path alone (no offset or limit).
steps.output: eia_raw_midwest.txt with the raw weekly dates and prices, plus the series ID, URL and retrieval date and the no-Indiana-series confirmation.
steps.done_when: eia_raw_midwest.txt exists on disk with at least 52 weekly date and price rows, and the series ID, URL, retrieval date and no-Indiana-series finding are stated.

steps.text: Build eia_midwest_diesel_52wk.csv from the saved raw file, with every row dated and cited, and write the gaps note.
steps.do: 1) Use local:Bash (grep, sed, head, tail) to select the 52 most recent consecutive Monday rows from eia_raw_midwest.txt; do not paste rows through context by hand. 2) Write eia_midwest_diesel_52wk.csv with columns week_date, price_usd_per_gal, series_id, source_url, retrieved_date, and fill the series ID, URL and retrieval date on every row. 3) Check with local:Bash that there are 52 data rows, the dates are 7 days apart, and the latest date is the latest release. 4) State the Midwest-as-Indiana-proxy note and any gaps or substitutes, each with a date.
steps.output: eia_midwest_diesel_52wk.csv (52 rows, columns week_date, price_usd_per_gal, series_id, source_url, retrieved_date) plus a gaps note that includes the proxy statement and dates.
steps.done_when: The CSV file exists with 52 consecutive weekly rows, each with price, series ID, URL and retrieval date; the proxy note is stated; every web figure carries a date; gaps and substitutes are written down.
